headline: Noise, plasticity, and connectivity each constrain neural representation
label: Constraints On Neural Representation
summary: Recent work formalizes correlated noise, presynaptic plasticity, and connectivity as explicit constraints on neural representation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that stochastic input, network connectivity, and synaptic learning rules each impose formal constraints on neural representation. A mean-field reduction of quadratic integrate-and-fire networks under correlated noise reports that correlation suppresses firing and induces metastability. An information-theoretic treatment of associative presynaptic short-term plasticity reports that release-probability rules enhance onset coding and recurrent replay. A published study finds that excitatory-only connectivity can amplify sequential assembly replay in spiking and membrane-potential population models. A third preprint introduces a Gaussian-equivalent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise replacement with lognormal moment closure to obtain a closed dynamical mean-field theory for noisy recurrent networks. What is new is the explicit treatment of each level as a constraint on representation; the items do not yet connect noise, plasticity, and connectivity directly.
